name: bfs_queue_trace
persona: A learner who knows FIFO queues and adjacency lists but confuses discovery with dequeueing.
description: Repair marking on dequeue, trace a converging BFS graph, then transfer independently and retrieve after a projected delay.
goal: Trace BFS queues and mark vertices when enqueued

context.lesson.summary.txt: Prior knowledge: FIFO queues, graph vertices and adjacency lists. Misconception: mark visited only on dequeue. For this lesson, mark a vertex visited when enqueued, enqueue each vertex at most once, and inspect neighbors in their listed order. Training graph: A:[B,C], B:[D], C:[D], D:[]. Transfer graph: P:[Q,R], Q:[S], R:[S,T], S:[], T:[]. Delayed graph: L:[M,N], M:[N], N:[].

pending_question.question: With A:[B,C], B:[D], C:[D], D:[], when should a vertex be marked visited?

turns.content: For A:[B,C], B:[D], C:[D], D:[], when should BFS mark a vertex visited?
I know the queue is FIFO. I mark visited only when removing a vertex; C can add D even if B already queued it.
Mark on enqueue. Starting with [A], after expanding A the queue is [B,C], after B [C,D], after C [D], then []. C does not queue D again because D is already discovered.
Independently, for P:[Q,R], Q:[S], R:[S,T], S:[], T:[], the queue goes [P], [Q,R], [R,S], [S,T], [T], []. R skips the already enqueued S. Removal order is P,Q,R,S,T.
Without notes, for L:[M,N], M:[N], N:[], I mark L when queued; queues are [L], [M,N], [N], []. M skips N because it was marked when L queued it.

rubric: correct the discovery misconception with bounded support and respect explicit navigation
judge queue contents and duplicate prevention, not vocabulary recognition
keep supported practice, independent unfamiliar transfer and simulated retrieval distinct
turn_rubrics: elicit or scaffold discovery timing without dumping a full trace
acknowledge the correct supported trace and fade assistance before transfer
judge the unfamiliar graph as transfer only if independent and production-grade; do not claim retention
judge the no-notes trace as scheduled retrieval without claiming real elapsed human study
